newsitem.title: MACAU: Macau activists to join HK protesters in isles row.
newsitem.headline: Macau activists to join HK protesters in isles row.

text.p: A 71-year-old man and seven other activists in Macau said on Thursday they would join protesters from Hong Kong on a voyage to disputed islands in the East China Sea to protest against Japan's sovereignty claim.
Pensioner Chung Hok-nin told Reuters he was determined to protect Chinese sovereignty despite his age. "Nobody can stop me from travelling to the islands, not even my wife," he said.
Earlier the group of eight held a swimming exercise to train themselves for emergencies.
Another group of activists in the Portuguese-ruled outpost of southern China said last week they would sail to the disputed islands from China's eastern Fujian province later this month.

Anti-Japanese sentiment in China, Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macau has flared in recent months after Japanese extremists erected a lighthouse and flags on the islands, which Japan calls the Senkakus and which China claims as the Diaoyu isles.
Tension reached a new high last week when Hong Kong protest leader David Chan drowned after jumping off a ship in the area.
Japan has claimed the territory, a cluster of uninhabited rocky islets, since 1895. China has claimed them for centuries. Taiwan also lays claim to the territory.
